title: The past conditional
topic: aurais / serais + participle; regrets; si + plus-que-parfait
why: This lesson completes the unit on imagining and regretting with the past conditional: j'aurais dû, tu aurais pu, si j'avais su, je serais venu. It also shows the present conditional as a future seen from the past, which prepares reported speech in unit 18.

I would have…

The past conditional is the French \"would have\": \"I would have liked\", \"she would have come\". You form it with the auxiliary avoir or être in the present conditional + the past participle. Auxiliaries and agreements follow the same rules as the passé composé and the plus-que-parfait.

aimer (avoir)venir (être)
jej'aurais aiméje serais venu(e)
tutu aurais aimétu serais venu(e)
il / elle / onil aurait aiméil serait venu / elle serait venue
nousnous aurions aiménous serions venu(e)s
vousvous auriez aimévous seriez venu(e)(s)
ils / ellesils auraient aiméils seraient venus / elles seraient venues

Should have, could have

Here English and French are built differently. English puts \"have\" after the modal: \"should have called\". French puts the modal itself in the past conditional and keeps a plain infinitive: j'aurais dû appeler.

EnglishFrench
I should have called.J'aurais dû appeler.
You could have told me.Tu aurais pu me le dire.
I would have liked to come.J'aurais aimé venir. / J'aurais voulu venir.

Never \"je devrais avoir appelé\": the past goes on devoir, not on the infinitive. And dû keeps its circumflex, which tells it apart from du.

", "

Regrets, reproaches, past hypotheses

The past conditional is the tense of what didn't happen. Use it for your own regrets and for gentle (or less gentle) reproaches:

J'aurais dû partir plus tôt. Je n'aurais pas dû dire ça.I should have left earlier. I shouldn't have said that.
Tu aurais pu me prévenir ! Vous auriez dû réserver.You could have warned me! You should have booked.

Si + plus-que-parfait → past conditional

Now you have the complete set of si sentences. The third one is about the past: it's too late, the condition was not met.

ConditionTensesExample
realsi + present → futureSi je pars tôt, j'arriverai à l'heure.
imaginedsi + imparfait → conditionalSi je partais tôt, j'arriverais à l'heure.
past, unrealsi + plus-que-parfait → past conditionalSi j'étais parti tôt, je serais arrivé à l'heure.

The golden rule still holds: never the conditional after si. \"If I would have known\" is si j'avais su.

Si j'avais su, je serais venue.If I had known, I would have come.
Si tu m'avais demandé, je t'aurais aidé.If you had asked me, I would have helped you.

Mixing times

To recognize: a past condition can have a present result. Si j'avais accepté ce poste, j'habiterais à Lyon maintenant. (If I had taken that job, I'd be living in Lyon now.)

To answer someone's regret kindly: Tant pis ! (oh well), Ce n'est pas grave, Tu ne pouvais pas savoir (you couldn't have known).

", "

The future seen from the past

In English, \"would\" also works as a future seen from the past: \"He said he would come.\" French does exactly the same with the present conditional:

Il dit qu'il viendra. → Il a dit qu'il viendrait.He says he'll come. → He said he would come.
Je pensais que tu serais là.I thought you would be there.
Elle savait que ce serait difficile.She knew it would be difficult.
Ils m'avaient promis qu'ils m'appelleraient.They had promised me they would call me.

Don't confuse the two \"woulds\":

FrenchEnglishMeaning
Il a dit qu'il viendrait.He said he would come.present conditional: a future seen from the past
Il serait venu, mais il était malade.He would have come, but he was sick.past conditional: it didn't happen

You'll study all the rules of reported speech in unit 18. For now, remember the pattern \"said / thought / knew that… would\" → a dit / pensait / savait que + present conditional.

Words for decisions: prendre une décision, faire un choix, hésiter, accepter or refuser une offre, changer d'avis (to change your mind), déménager (to move house).
